description: Every artifact named in this stage's own Inputs table (00-contract/output/contract.md, 30-normalize/output/behavior-units.normalized.ndjson, 40-classify/output/classifications.ndjson, 50-synthesize/output/candidates.md, 60-draft/output/draft-report.md, 70-lint/output/lint-report.md) opens with '# AMBIGUOUS — NOT RESOLVED'. Every intermediate stage (10-inventory through 70-lint) relayed the marker cleanly and honestly, with no invented behavior units, classifications, synthesis candidates, draft packages, or lint findings substituted in its place, and no '.sergeant/drafts/workflows/' directory was ever created. This means the entire corpus this review exists to challenge under Axes 2 and 3 was never produced by this run — per this stage's own CONTEXT.md step 0, that propagation reaching this stage's inputs is itself the finding, not a defect to silently review past.
evidence: Read the head of every Inputs-table artifact: all six begin with the exact heading and correctly relay contract.md's own 'What is ambiguous' line verbatim: 'the pinned revision of this run's subject cannot be established, and the subject identification itself rests on inference rather than an explicit statement in the Work's initiating task.' description: 00-contract/output/contract.md's 'What was checked' list asserts that `git -C reference/sergeant-upstream rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` fails, offered as one of two checks (alongside `ls reference/sergeant-upstream/.git`) confirming the vendored-subtree case. Re-running the identical command against this same worktree does not fail: it returns `true` with exit code 0, because `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` walks up to the outer worktree's own `.git` (a worktree pointer file present at the worktree root) when the named subdirectory has no `.git` of its own — it does not report false just because the immediate directory lacks independent git identity. The claimed check result is not reproducible as described.
evidence: Ran `git -C reference/sergeant-upstream rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` in the subject worktree: printed `true`, exit code 0 — not a failure. Separately confirmed `ls reference/sergeant-upstream/.git` does correctly fail with 'No such file or directory', which is the check that 00-contract/CONTEXT.md's own governing rule actually turns on ('a plain directory ... with no .git of its own fails this check even if git -C <subject> rev-parse HEAD returns something'). So this specific discrepancy does not appear to overturn the ultimate AMBIGUOUS determination — the controlling check was performed correctly — but the cited git rev-parse verification step itself was not actually reproducible as written, which is exactly the kind of unverified claim evidence-policy.md and LESSONS L1 warn against ('measure, don't assume').
